item.title: Overcoming Fear: What Open Water Swimming Taught Me
item.description: Of the three legs of a triathlon, swimming is the one that scares me most. Notes on why open water breaks down control, and what building competence, staying present, and accepting the worst case actually do to fear.

item.title: It's Not Rocket Science: Designing an AI Computer That Scales
item.description: The hardest part of chip architecture was never mastering some arcane secret — it’s deciding what to do and what not to do under real constraints. The question is how to design a computer that can actually be used at scale, not a machine that only works with the most advanced process node, the deepest pockets, and the most specialized team.

item.title: Hooding and Notes from Work
item.description: Parents in town for hooding and travel—notes from my first real break after work on why shipping silicon is largely a management problem, slow feedback loops in hardware, the mindset behind heavy AI use, and why we need a better AI computer, not a faster niche accelerator.

item.title: April Fools, Fitness Coaching, and Two Real Questions
item.description: An April Fools prank sparked two genuine questions — am I pursuing what makes me happy, and has AI actually made humanity happier?

item.title: The Motorcycle and the Zen: Reading Notes
item.description: Care is on the human side, Quality is on the object side, and engagement is the thread connecting them. Reading notes on Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance.

item.title: ARM, RISC-V, and AI
item.description: Three questions on the ARM vs. RISC-V battle — what RISC-V actually has going for it in the AI era, why ARM is now making its own SoC, and where RISC-V still has ground to cover.

item.title: Why I Always Show Up at the Office
item.description: It is not just about separating work from life — it is about not missing the serendipitous collisions that only happen in person.

item.title: Computer Architecture Is Entering a Golden Era
item.description: AI-native workloads, edge fragmentation, and faster experimentation are pushing architecture back to the center of hardware value creation.

item.title: Experience
item.description:
Work Experience

Senior Architect — Tenstorrent Inc

Santa Clara, California · May 2025 – Present

Architected NoC, D2D, and memory-system tradeoff studies across chiplet-based AI/ML accelerator systems, including GDDR, LPDDR, IO, and RISC-V CPU chiplets. Drove decisions across routing, QoS, topology, clocking, and debug visibility to close throughput, latency, utilization, power, and area goals. Defined requirements for links, queues, memory channels, and address interleaving, using performance analysis where it materially improved architecture decisions. Debugged cross-stack performance and power issues with RTL, physical design, verification, and software teams. Led architecture reviews spanning non-coherent NoCs, AXI/CHI/PCIe fabrics, chiplet interconnects, and LPDDR/DDR subsystem interactions.

item.title: Semiconductor Development Cycles Will Shrink Faster Than Expected
item.description: As prototyping, validation, and silicon feedback loops shrink from months to days, chip development will start to move at a cadence much closer to software.

item.title: Using AI Well Starts with Redesigning the Workflow
item.description: Getting real leverage from AI requires more than adding a model to existing processes. It requires rethinking workflow design, sign-off cost, and the role of infrastructure.

item.title: Saying No Is a Commitment to Your Long-Term Goals
item.description: Setting boundaries and saying no is not cold-hearted; it is how you protect focus for what matters most.

item.title: From Book Smart and Street Smart to System Smart
item.description: For complex projects, isolated skills are not enough; scalable systems set the ceiling.

item.title: Zipper: Latency-Tolerant Optimizations for High-Performance Buses
item.description: Zipper is a protocol optimization layer that reduces bus communication latency by enabling device and request level parallelism and exploiting data locality — achieving 8x speedup with under 5% logic overhead.

item.title: Security Verification of Low-Trust Architectures
item.description: A complete formal verification of the Sequestered Encryption (SE) low-trust architecture, proving security against direct data disclosures and digital side channels for all possible programs, demonstrated across seven correct and buggy RTL implementations.

item.title: Twine: A Chisel Extension for Component-Level Heterogeneous Design
item.description: Twine is a Chisel extension that standardizes hardware component interfaces and supports control-free specification with flexible data type conversion, considerably improving reusability for heterogeneous designs.

item.title: Morpheus: A Vulnerability-Tolerant Secure Architecture Based on Ensembles of Moving Target Defenses with Churn
item.description: Morpheus is a RISC-V secure architecture that combines ensembles of moving target defenses with churn to continuously re-randomize pointers and code, achieving high-coverage protection against control-flow attacks with negligible (1%) performance overhead.

item.title: CommPact: Evaluating the Feasibility of Autonomous Vehicle Contracts
item.description: CommPact proposes Autonomous Vehicle contracts using Intel SGX secure enclaves to enforce agreed-upon driving rules in platoons, allowing safe contract termination within 1.5 seconds of an attack.
